title: Protocol and Archive
premise: Mara Yarrow is sent to audit the 'impossible' insurance losses of Meridian Deep, a mining colony officially abandoned years ago but secretly still alive, sustained by forged reports and a shared fiction that two rival fleets are already at war over its ruins. When the colony's children begin dreaming the same dream — of a beacon singing beneath the ice — Mara realizes the lie holding the fleets apart is fraying, and she must choose between filing the truth and protecting the people who have become her family. With her estranged fleet-officer brother arriving to enforce evacuation, Mara and the colonists stage one final broadcast, feeding both fleets a fabricated catastrophe so terrible neither dares approach. The book ends with Meridian Deep erased from every official record but alive in secret, Mara staying behind as its new archivist, having traded duty for belonging.
about_author: Hazel Nystrom is a former maritime claims adjuster who spent a decade investigating losses at sea before turning to fiction about people who survive being written off. She writes from a coastal town where fog is frequent and records, she insists, should never be fully trusted.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Fires
chapters.summary: Mara Yarrow arrives at Meridian Deep expecting ghosts and finds three hundred living colonists maintaining elaborate fictions for her benefit. Through her POV, we see her professional suspicion war with unexpected warmth as engineer Sef Okafor shows her the colony's hidden hydroponics. The emotional beat is reluctant wonder: an investigator trained to find fraud discovering a fraud worth protecting.

chapters.title: What the Children Dream
chapters.summary: Mara's POV continues as eleven children independently describe an identical dream: a beacon under the ice, singing coordinates. When she verifies the signal exists, panic ripples through the colony's leadership — the dream means the buried transmitter is waking, and it will summon both fleets. The emotional beat shifts from curiosity to dread; belonging now has a countdown attached.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Lie
chapters.summary: Mara's brother, Commander Ivo Yarrow, arrives with the Concordat fleet demanding evacuation and truth. Told partly from Ivo's POV, the chapter escalates as Mara feeds him doctored sensor data while the children's dream spreads to adults — the whole colony now dreaming together. Climax builds as Ivo discovers her forgery, forcing Mara to confess everything and ask him to join the lie.

chapters.title: Erasure, Sung
chapters.summary: In the climax, the colonists detonate their own transmitter and broadcast a fabricated plague outbreak, convincing both fleets that Meridian Deep must be quarantined forever. Ivo, choosing his sister over his commission, falsifies the final report. In the quiet resolution, Mara burns her investigation files and accepts the archivist's post, finally home among the people everyone else forgot.
